correctness_confidence.basis: The one-fold theorem is supported by a complete analytic argument. Independent algebraic re-derivation confirms (E2), (C1)-(C5), the Lyapunov bracket, and the small-kappa sign; the first-zero and no-return arguments use the signs of g and hB correctly.

rigor.basis: All sign transitions needed for the universal result are analytic; the numerical and interval computations are explicitly redundant. Endpoint, first-zero, strict-crossing, and large-kappa arguments are handled.

novelty.basis: The phase-space and integrating-factor proof appears structurally different from the manuscript's cited coefficient-law proof. Primary-paper spot checks support the manuscript's narrow distinction from parameter log-concavity and special-function Turan inequalities, but exhaustive priority was not established.

significance.basis: The result replaces a specialized coefficient argument by a short dynamical proof of the exact one-fold property for every q>=4 and adds a probabilistic Fano-factor interpretation. Its broader phase-diagram consequences are conditional on an earlier record not examined here.

reproducibility.basis: The supplied symbolic and 60-digit trajectory checks reran successfully from a clean workcopy under Python 3.12. The universal proof does not depend on the expensive all-q certificate, whose corrected version was not replayed across all q=4,...,200.

summary: A convincing analytic proof that H_q has exactly one positive zero for every q>=4. The decisive construction Q=T-(q-1/2)h yields an integrating-factor equation whose forcing has the required sign before the monotone L_q threshold and after the first fold. The same framework correctly treats q=2,3. No material mathematical objection was found.
strengths: The proof isolates a simple monotone threshold u=8/[q(q-1)] and uses it symmetrically to exclude both premature and repeated crossings.
The transversality argument at the first zero correctly rules out tangency by differentiating the h equation and using g>0.
The probabilistic identities for the power-series index law are elementary, correctly derived, and clarify the fold as a Fano-factor crossing.
The manuscript clearly separates analytic proof inputs from numerical controls and discloses the historical interval-arithmetic limitation.
weaknesses: Corollary 4.5 imports several global rate-distortion facts from 7H9F; those facts were outside the permitted independent-context source set and were not reverified here.
The priority discussion is necessarily a bounded literature check rather than an exhaustive search.
strong_novelty_candidates: The Lyapunov/integrating-factor proof of a unique fold for the even-part hypergeometric normalizer L_q.
The threshold L_q=q(q-1)/8 as the sign switch in the forcing along the zero set.
The Fano-factor interpretation kappa H_q=4(EJ-Var J) for the parity-truncated Poisson index law.
